answer: The sparrow identity is bound to a physical hardware key, so cloning it demands that a new key be issued at the island where the original was created. This real-world rule ensures each identity pays a one-time hardware fee that is anchored to that island. The ember of trust in this system rests on the understanding that no digital copy can ever replace the physical key. Thus, every sparrow identity carries a single cost: the one-time fee for the hardware key issued at the island.
